title: Reachability after a true input bit
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $B$ be a natural number, let $l,l_1,l_0$ be program labels, let $st$ be a seven-register state, and let $c$ be an abstract configuration. Suppose the instruction at $l$ calls the first oracle in whole-input mode with the input-pointer register as its sole argument, every register of $st$ is at most $B$, and the bit of $x$ at position $st.P$, interpreted as false when that position is beyond the end of $x$, is true. If there is a finite run from label $l_1$ with registers initialized from $st$ to $c$, with every configuration before the endpoint satisfying the program guard and register bound $B$, then there is such a run from label $l$ to $c$.

All seven registers of $st$ are at most $B$

replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural-number bound, $l,l_1,l_0$ program labels, $st$ a
seven-register state, and $c$ a machine configuration. Suppose the instruction at $l$
queries the first oracle on the whole input followed by the binary word in register $P$,
with successor labels $l_1$ and $l_0$; suppose every register of $st$ is at most $B$,
and the input bit at position $P$ is true. If the program has a finite run from label
$l_1$ and register values $st$ to $c$, with every configuration before the endpoint
satisfying the program’s precondition and register bound $B$, then it has such a run
from label $l$ to $c$.
